findings.title: try/catch no longer protects calendar/video deletions after switching to async forEach
findings.body: The forEach callback is now `async` and awaits `getCalendar`. Its promise is never awaited, so the surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) cannot catch errors from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting`. Before this change, `getCalendar` was synchronous, so its throws were caught here. Now any failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection, which can crash the process on Node or log noise, and the error handler that logs via `logger.error` is dead code.

findings.title: Same regression: try/catch is ineffective around async forEach, errors become unhandled rejections
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` with `await getCalendar(...)` inside a try block. The callbacks are not awaited and the try/catch cannot observe their rejections, so calendar deletion failures are no longer logged and surface as unhandled promise rejections. The function also returns `true` before these deletions settle, so their outcome is never observed.

findings.title: forEach(async) pushes to apiDeletes after the array has already been awaited
findings.body: In the recurring-cancel branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })` does not await the callbacks. Later `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` and the `await apiDeletes` in the payment branch run while those pushes may not have happened yet. Calendar deletions can therefore be skipped from the awaited set, and their errors are unhandled.

findings.title: Errors from getCalendar in CalendarManager.getCalendarCredentials are not handled
findings.body: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts, `getCalendarCredentials` calls `getCalendar(credential)` without await and stores the resulting promise. Since `getCalendar` is now async, a rejection (for example from the CalendarService constructor) is unhandled until `item.calendar` is awaited, which may never happen for credentials filtered out downstream.

findings.title: appStore values are now Promises; any caller that does not await them silently breaks
findings.body: Every entry of `appStore` changed from a module namespace to a `Promise` returned by `import()`. Any consumer that indexes `appStore[...]` and uses `.lib` without awaiting now gets a Promise, so `"lib" in app` is false and features are silently disabled, with no type error if the consumer relies on inferred types. Only the call sites shown in this diff were updated. Other consumers of `appStore` (for example `packages/app-store/utils`, `locations`, or web API routes) must be audited, and the PR description does not mention this breaking change.

findings.title: Adapters are loaded sequentially in a loop, serializing dynamic imports
findings.body: `getVideoAdapters` awaits each `appStore[...]` import one at a time inside `for ... of`. The previous code was synchronous and the imports are independent, so `Promise.all` over the credentials would avoid serializing the module loads on every busy-time or meeting operation.
